reasons: Covers completions, plans, budgets, estimates, baselines and name splitting in several languages.
Uses fixed examples and runs without outside services.

terms.meaning: The original approved plan that later results are compared against.
Actually happened, as opposed to planned or forecast.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test imports
sections.what: Brings in the test runner, the assertion helper, the field support check and the reported role check.
sections.why: Likely reason: each test calls these checks directly.

sections.name: ok (part 1)
sections.title: Tests dates and budgets in several languages
sections.what: Runs real-style sentences in German, Finnish, Dutch, Norwegian, Swedish and English. Checks that completion wording counts only when the completion is stated as done and the month is written. Checks that plans and forecasts never count, that budgets count only with an approval or reported final cost, and that estimates never count as final costs.
sections.why: The comment ties these expectations to role words approved on 2026-10-29, so each case records an approved rule.
sections.watch_out: Expectations encode a decision about which wording is acceptable, so they should change only with the owner's agreement.

sections.name: ok (part 2)
sections.title: Tests name splitting for source names
sections.what: Checks that a recorded name with brackets expands into the forms a source might print, and that short, descriptive or place-qualifier brackets are not treated as names.
sections.why: Likely reason: mistakes here would let a place name stand in for a project name.
sections.watch_out: Expected lists are exact, so a change in ordering or wording of the output fails the test.

summary: Automated tests that check the role words accept the right sentences in each source language and reject plans, forecasts and estimates.
purpose: Protects the wording rules that decide whether a quote supports a budget, completion date or schedule baseline.
why: Likely reason: the word lists are long and easy to break, so tests catch an accidental loss of accepted or rejected wording.
how: Runs real-style quotes in several languages through the field check and the reported-role check, and compares each result to the expected yes or no. Also checks the name-splitting rules.
inputs: Fixed quotes, values and amounts written inside the file.
outputs: Pass or fail for each test.
risks: Expectations reflect decisions about acceptable wording, so changing one changes what the report accepts.
debug: If a case flips, read which word list it touches in roleWords.ts, then check whether the change was meant. Each test names the rule it checks.
